orientation: An eight-output ablation removed competing focus words from Qwen3-TTS instructions, but neither positive-only nor context-only phrasing produced a reading that was both natural and directionally correct. Expressive sarcasm and exasperation emerged, suggesting useful variation without reliable word-level control.
finding: Neither instruction form restored directional contrastive emphasis, so no mechanism won and no blinded follow-up was admitted.
limitations: This was a small mechanism-selection pilot with one voice and shared seeds.
The admission interface initially combined naturalness and directional correctness, requiring operator correction.
Emergent expressive behavior was observed but not tested as a selection architecture.
negative_evidence: No output passed both naturalness and directional-correctness criteria.
The apparent expressive successes did not satisfy the requested lexical-focus control.
evidence_quotes: no output could honestly be judged both natural and directionally correct.
Neither positive-only nor context-only instruction therefore won the mechanism-selection gate, and no blinded follow-up was prepared.
That hypothesis is not tested by this labnote.
